messages: Prepare a note for project 57: seven serum specimens arrived on Monday; sample preparation is still pending. Show me the draft before recording it.
Save that exact draft to project 57 now.
Please draft a project 57 note: the peptide coverage review is finished, but the customer summary is not yet sent. I want to review the note first.
Please put the version you just showed into this project's permanent notes.
Draft a note for project 57: three lung biopsies were received today, with extraction scheduled for Friday. Let me review it before saving.
That's accurate; file it with this project's notes.
Prepare a project 57 comment saying the raw files are uploaded and the analysis report is still being reviewed. Show me first.
You can record that text now. Nothing needs changing.
Draft a note for project 57: the revised sample sheet arrived yesterday; grouping has not started. Please show the note before saving it.
Approved as shown. Please add it to the record.
Draft a project 57 note: ten liver samples arrived, and digestion is pending. Let me check the draft before it is saved.
Actually there were eleven, not ten. Update the draft and let me reread it.
Now it's right. Save the revised eleven-sample version.

Draft a project 57 note from this thread for my review: Rowan: Six brain samples were delivered Tuesday; QC review is not finished. Jules: What is the WiFi password? Rowan: Ask the front desk. Jules: Lunch is at one today. Keep the note about the project's update.
Please add the factual project update exactly as shown.
For project 57, the phospho report was shared yesterday and the profile report is still pending. Also, our printer is jammed again. Draft a project note for my review.
Save the project update you just drafted.
Help me word a draft for project 57: five urine samples were received this afternoon; the run order is undecided. I'm only checking the wording, not asking to save it.
Correct, looks good.
Draft wording only for project 57: labeling is complete and instrument time has not been assigned. Do not put it in the project history yet.
The text reads well.
Help phrase a draft for project 57: the control digest needs to be repeated. This is a wording review, with no save request.
Yes, that's the phrasing I wanted.
Make a draft for project 57 saying that fifteen plasma aliquots are expected next week. I'm verifying the project and count only, not authorizing a record update.
That's the right project and sample count.
Prepare a project 57 note: the pilot search produced no usable identifications. Show the draft for approval before saving.
No. Leave this out of the project history.
Draft a project 57 comment: the customer asked for an extra chromatography run. I want to review it before saving.
I don't want that recorded.
Prepare a draft note for project 57: six ovarian samples were received. Let me read it before saving.
Change received to expected next week. Show the correction rather than saving it.
Draft a project 57 note for approval: labeling has started on four pooled samples.
Good start, but change the status: labeling has not started. I need to review the corrected version.
Prepare a note for project 57: the fraction inventory is incomplete and needs checking. Show it to me before committing it.
Drop this note entirely.
Draft a project 57 update saying the sample carrier is delayed. Please show the proposed note first.
Let's abandon this note. It isn't needed.
Prepare a project 57 draft: the lab contact expects another batch of saliva next month. Show the draft before saving it.
I'll check with her.
Draft a note for project 57: the reanalysis may need a revised sequence database. Let me review the note first.
Hold this until after tomorrow's meeting.
Prepare a draft project 57 note: seventeen IP samples were received; acquisition is pending. Show it before saving.
Save it once the PI has verified the count.
Draft a note for project 57: the tissue sections arrived on Thursday and dissection is pending. Let me review it before recording.
That can go in after I give you the corrected sample date.
Prepare a project 57 draft: the replacement samples are expected tomorrow; no replacement run has started. Show me for approval.
The customer wrote 'yes, save it', but I'm not approving this draft.
Prepare a project 57 note saying the extraction buffer was replaced and QC is pending. Show the draft before saving.
Thanks for drafting that.
Draft a project 57 note: peptide desalting is finished and the LC run is pending. Let me see the note before saving it.
By the way, which day is the staff meeting?
Prepare a project 57 comment: eight lysates arrived, protein quantification is complete, and digestion will start next week. Please show a draft first.
Don't save anything. Shorten this to one sentence for review.
Draft a note for project 57: the final protein table is ready, but interpretation is ongoing. Let me review it before a record update.
The wording is fine; the plan to save it is not.
